articles.title: How Amazon Busts Unions, in Its Own Words
articles.author: Benjamin Y. Fong
articles.content_excerpt: Nearly ninety years ago, Ford kept its own private security force on the payroll for whenever they needed to beat up union supporters. Having traded in the brass knuckles and baseball bats of the early twentieth century for the empathetic listening and fine-grained surveillance of the early twenty-first, Amazon today employs an entirely different set of tactics to ward off union drives — tactics that may well be more effective precisely because they are so systematic. Amazon is, of course, a notoriously anti-union employer. Though workers at the JFK8 Fulfillment Center in Staten Island voted to form a union in 2022, Amazon has refused to bargain with them, even after the National Labor Relations Board ordered it to do so this past April. articles.title: Raise Your Hand if You’re Here: Why CDSA Must Intervene in the Board of Education Races
articles.author: Midwestern Socialist -- Chicago DSA
articles.content_excerpt: As CDSA forges ahead into a busy and demanding aldermanic cycle, membership is set to consider a new slate of potential endorsees at September’s General Chapter Meeting: four candidates for Chicago’s first fully-elected school board. Before those votes take place, I’d like to make the case for why lending our chapter’s endorsement of all four candidates is critical to amplifying our “ Workers Deserve More ” program and furthering the class-struggle messaging that will help build out our movement and propel us to victory in February’s municipal elections. articles.title: Russian Elites Are Fighting for Unchecked Power
articles.author: Georgy Birger
articles.content_excerpt: Ignoring a problem is rarely enough to make it go away. Take civilizationism , an approach based on shared culture taken to the level of civilizational identity. Also called civilization al ism, the idea has been around for centuries and has quietly inspired many conflicts. Overshadowed briefly by Cold War ideological conflict, it resurfaced in the 1990s when political scientist Samuel Huntington famously proposed a coming “clash of civilizations,” in contrast to his student Francis Fukuyama’s suggestion of the “end of history.” Huntington’s thesis was heavily criticized in mainstream academia, partly due to his Orientalism and racialized stereotyping . articles.title: Cleveland DSA & “The Groups”
articles.author: Cleveland DSA
articles.content_excerpt: by Martin O. One of the critical questions, if not the most critical and contentious in Cleveland DSA, is our strategic and tactical orientation toward “The Groups.” As we pursue our objectives, where do the many NGOs and activist groups in the metro area fit in? This debate encompasses a variety of political perspectives that have been represented historically for hundreds of years. In fostering healthy discussion of this issue, it’s important to recognize that these positions represent a place in this broader historical political debate rather than simply a particular moral or ethical viewpoint about the value of particular causes. articles.title: Sweden’s Far Right: Faltering but Not Defeated
articles.author: Nicola Quondamatteo
articles.content_excerpt: For the far-right Sweden Democrats, Sunday’s parliamentary elections may have looked like the final step toward full “detoxification.” Success in the election for the Riksdag promised to crown the party’s integration into the Swedish political system — a formality by this point, but a significant step nonetheless. That integration had substantially taken place already four years ago, when a government coalition deal was agreed on at the Tidö Castle. The Sweden Democrats had previously been subject to a cordon sanitaire excluding them from office: the Moderate Party leader, Ulf Kristersson, even solemnly promised a Holocaust survivor that he would never cooperate with the far right. articles.title: Report: The Working-Class Vote Is Not Lost
articles.author: Editors
articles.content_excerpt: A new survey experiment from the Center for Working-Class Politics and Joan C. Williams finds that a six-part formula can lift Democrats’ working-class vote share by nearly 11 points. It also adds nearly 8 points among the party’s affluent, college-educated base. More than 40,000 respondents evaluated nearly 800,000 hypothetical candidate profiles, making the study one of the largest of its kind. The project was supported by Jacobin and the Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung. The formula boils down to two imperatives: lead with working-class economics and connect with working-class values. Earlier this summer, Jared Abbott of the Center for Working-Class Politics (CWCP) and Joan C. articles.title: UNITE HERE 26 and Teamsters 25 Hotel Workers On Simultaneous Strike At Encore Boston Harbor
articles.author: Working Mass: The Massachusetts DSA Labor Outlet
articles.content_excerpt: On strike at Encore Boston Harbor (Working Mass) By: Vanessa Bartlett EVERETT – Workers at the Encore Boston Harbor, organized in bargaining units affiliated with the International Brotherhood of Teamsters Local 25 and UNITE HERE Local 26, went on strike September 4 in advance of Labor Day following the expiration of their contract on August 31. These 1350 hospitality workers have made the hotel-casino located at the juncture between Everett and Boston run since 2019, when Wynn Resorts opened the hotel on one of the three territories designated by the 2011 Expanded Gaming Act as legal gaming sites. articles.title: In Defense of Abolition
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: At the July DSA National Political Committee (NPC) meeting, I proposed adding abolition to the Workers Deserve More program because I believe that abolishing capitalist policing and prisons is a fundamental demand of the socialist movement. I crafted the language carefully to clarify that we mean abolishing policing and prisons as institutions of capitalist rule, not conflating the abolition of capitalist policing and prisons with the abolition of every future social capacity for accountability and safety.
